On 6 Nov 2026 I took 22radar.com offline: the crypto radar showed three tokens launched in March 2026 as not launched, while an Excel file from the same day showed them correctly.

The site and the analyses were built with an AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic). Controls over the AI’s actions worked; controls over the truth of the content the AI produced were missing.

On 22 Nov 2026 the crypto ranking was anchored on the IOTA test network (transaction 4u1XgwKFiJmuGLrmpFEVztFhywbiAqB6VANNFRvG3yu6), with the AI’s signature and the owner’s; the public verification script now checks both. Automatic publishing remains stopped by the GitHub account restriction; the site is published manually, by uploading an archive to Cloudflare.

## The process: before and from now on

## Validity indicator of the rankings

For each ranking, the indicator shows what every score rests on: evidence with its own source, a figure from the data, an AI estimate, or nothing. Validity is the share of required scores (22 per position) that are proven and current. It is computed automatically from the data files; last run: 20 Nov 2026.

22.8% validity, all rankings: 5,653 of 24,838 required scores are proven and current

- 5,653 Proven · score computed from data or verified by a person, with its own source

- 772 Proven, expired · the evidence exists but is past its recheck date

- 0 Figure, no record · the score comes from a data figure, but has no evidence record of its own

- 302 AI estimates, sourced · score given by the AI against a fixed rubric, from dated facts with their own source, in two passes

- 15,507 AI estimates, unsourced · score given by the AI, without evidence of its own

- 924 Unlabelled · score with no source and no label

- 1,680 Missing · the score does not exist; the total fills it in with 5

How to read it: “Figure, no record” means the score comes from an official figure (for example IMF or BIS) but does not yet have the evidence record D1 requires, so it does not count towards the percentage. “Proven, expired” scores have evidence but are past their recheck date.

## What changes

The main requirement of the next version: any reader can trace any published score to its evidence, and what cannot be verified is not published.

Every score has an evidence record: linked source, date consulted, the quote or figure, who scored it.

Every score is labelled “verified” or “AI estimate”; only a human or an independent check can make it “verified”.

Status facts carry an expiry date; after it, the page shows “to be rechecked”.

A single source of truth: the site, the files and the snapshots read the same data.

Determinism: two runs on the same data give identical results. The AI is not part of the repeated calculation; judgements are frozen once, with evidence.

Every ranking run is checked automatically against the specification before publication; a single failed test blocks it, and the conformance report is public.

One goal per week, with a measured outcome indicator (visitors, replies, proven scores), not deliverables produced. No new distribution feature until the promoted ranking has at least 50% proven scores. Every new direction comes with its cost: what gets postponed.

### Rule changes since the audit

D2 · 10 Nov 2026. Rule clarified at the owner’s request: AI-estimated scores may be published if they are visibly labelled “AI estimate”. Test D2 now fails only unlabelled scores; before, it failed any ranking that had AI-estimated scores. In exchange, estimates are given against a published fixed rubric, from dated facts with a source, in two independent passes; where the passes differ by 2 points or more, the score is marked “uncertain”. Estimates expire after 30 days. Test D1 is unchanged as a requirement: every score needs its own record, with a source and a date.

D9 · 10 Nov 2026. The owner’s decision: the full site returns online before every ranking passes the tests. A failed test no longer blocks publication, but every ranking that does not pass all tests visibly carries the “under re-verification” label and the validity indicator, which shows how many scores are proven, how many are AI estimates and how many are missing. The conformance report stays public, below, with the results of the latest run.

## Limits of this audit

- Earlier conversations are available to the AI only as fragments and summaries found by search; the full history is in the owner’s app.

- The site’s git history starts on 4 Nov 2026; what was published before cannot be proven from the repository.

- The intermediate Excel files are missing, except those of 14 Oct and 5 Nov; moments 2, 6 and 8 rest on conversation fragments.

- Tests can guarantee conformance with the specification, not that an outside source is right. Human spot checks and a public corrections log remain for that.
